comparisonOrder.decides: Real reflected coast attaches to the bank at the correct position and orientation; flat control is optical evidence, not the intended wave appearance.
Depth-guided wave distortion breaks up the mirror naturally without losing coherent coast contact or creating stretched stripes.
Recently wetted exposed sand remains glossy while older damp sand loses its broad polished ribbon; assess the independent film change.
Film change still helps with real coast reflection active; the two features do not hide each other's defects.
The combined improvement survives a nearby real route/wave time. Both members use t10.75; comparison to t10.5 includes camera motion and is not a temporal-stability proof.
Decoded RGBA must match exactly after both studies and a time seek. Any difference is unresolved state restoration, not acceptable artistic variation.

opticalFailureChecks: Reflection: no mirrored land above the waterline, underwater geometry leak, missing/inverted coast, duplicate coast edge, rectangular capture boundary, black stripe, bright alpha halo or separate pasted-looking mirror surface.

Reflection: no global sky/exposure/color change, double fog veil, canopy coverage thickening, clipped-tree fragments, overblurred coast smear, or plausible-looking dark stripe unrelated to actual visible coast.

Distortion: coast remains geographically connected as wave normals vary; no stretched triangles, hard depth-classification edge, divergent sampling flash or glaring jump to sky at the capture boundary. Downward rays retain the existing neighbouring-water fallback.

Film: only exposed sand gloss is shortened. The damp color boundary, actual waterline, sand geometry, vegetation, sky and offshore foam remain coherent; freshly wetted sand must not become chalky/matte and older damp sand must not change hue.

Cross-feature: above-water land/sky composition and shadow placement remain stable. A main-camera LOD/packing change, missing tree or retained mirrored camera is a rejection regardless of prettier water.
requiredRuntimeEvidence: No shader, context, network or capture-health errors; same current sourceIdentity and 640x360 output throughout.

Reflection ON stats: enabled=true, initialized=true, ready=true, width=320, height=180, samples=4, distortion equals entry. OFF/restored stats: enabled=false and ready=false. Cached resources may remain initialized while OFF.
All frames use debug0, native output with linearMainOutput=false and sampleScale1. Record per-frame settings and reflection state from the existing capture manifest.
Compare decoded RGBA for the restored pair, not PNG byte hashes alone. Keep timing/call/triangle records descriptive; this eight-image plan is not a speed benchmark.
decisionRule: Reject any optical or restored-state failure. Reflection, drying and combined appearance receive separate yes/no decisions from the isolated pairs. A subtle improvement is a narrow study result; these stills cannot establish an 8/10 result or authorize a full-film default change.
